subject.title: [Feature Request] Hook Chain Integrity Protection Against Message Tampering

question: What security guarantee should OpenClaw provide for mutable plugin hooks: audit-only provenance for trusted in-process plugins, enforced integrity for isolated plugins, or one permission model spanning both?
rationale: In-process plugins share core authority, while isolation, audit retention, and hook authorization alter security and compatibility contracts that source inspection cannot choose safely.

options.title: Boundary-aware design
options.body: Add typed permissions and redacted provenance generally, but enforce cryptographic integrity only across a host-controlled isolation boundary.

options.title: Audit and permissions only
options.body: Add mutation audit records and fine-grained authorization without claiming tamper prevention for in-process plugins.

options.title: Defer until isolation
options.body: Retain current behavior until plugin process isolation provides a meaningful enforcement boundary.

recommendation.title: Boundary-aware design
recommendation.body: Add typed permissions and redacted provenance generally, but enforce cryptographic integrity only across a host-controlled isolation boundary.
